description: For a learner who can make attempts at a new concept or principle, exploration guided by clues, questions on the learner's own ideas and critique of everyone's work, with the principle then named from that work, is expected to deepen understanding more than being told first or exploring unguided, though no claim tests indirect against direct guidance.
title: Understanding must be cultivated through exploration, not described or told

description: For a class whose learners vary in access, language, prior knowledge and motivation, planning several routes into content, engagement and expression while the goal and criteria stay fixed is expected to let more learners reach the goal than a single-route design; no claim here tests UDL as a framework, only its parts.
title: Universal Design For Learning

description: In kindergarten to grade 3, briefly screening every child for early reading risk at set points in the year and following each flag within weeks with a diagnostic look and added instruction is expected to find children who need help sooner than referral; the wiki holds no test of screening itself, and its evidence (mostly one Massachusetts research programme) shows screeners flag later strugglers better than they clear the rest, disagree with each other, and flag children from low-income families, English learners and Black and Hispanic children more often, gaps that reflect circumstances, treatment and possibly the measure, not the children.
title: Universal Early Literacy Screening
